articles.title: Another major ad agency recommends pausing Twitter ad campaigns
articles.summary: Omnicom Media Group recommended that clients (which include Pepsi, Apple, and McDonald’s) pause advertising on Twitter, citing “potential serious implications” since Elon Musk’s takeover. It’s the second of the “big four” agencies to do so, following IPG.
articles.body: Omnicom, one of the world’s biggest ad firms, representing brands like McDonald’s, Apple, and PepsiCo, is recommending clients pause spending on Twitter, according to an internal memo obtained by The Verge. Omnicom Media Group is recommending clients “pause activity on Twitter in the short term,” according to a note titled “Twitter - Continued Brand Safety Concerns.” The memo cites recent events in the last few days that have “potential serious implications” for brands running ads on the platform. The memo cites the deep layoffs of Twitter trust and safety teams, the resignations of high-profile executives, and the slew of “verified” impersonation accounts as being key issues for advertisers. There is “evidence that the risk to our clients’ brand safety has risen sharply to a level most would find unacceptable,” the memo reads. “We recommend pausing activity on Twitter in the short term until the platform can prove it has reintroduced safeguards to an acceptable level and has regained control of its environment.” The memo goes on to say that Omnicom has “formally requested that Twitter assure us that these issues will not impact compliant processes, operations, products, brand safety and client investment on the platform in any way” but that “seemingly due to the lack of senior leadership now in these areas, Twitter has not been able to give those assurances.” It’s the latest in a string of advertisers that have changed plans following the chaos at Twitter since Elon Musk’s takeover. Last week, IPG, another ad agency giant, recommended its clients suspend their advertising on Twitter, according to CNBC. Companies like Volkswagen, General Motors, and General Mills have also pulled ad spending from Twitter in recent weeks. The majority of Twitter’s revenue comes from ads, and despite Musk’s questionable efforts at soothing their concerns, advertisers are worried about their content showing up next to an influx of hate speech and impersonations. They’re also concerned about Musk’s own tweets, like his threats to “thermonuclear name & shame” advertisers who pull their money from the platform. In Musk’s first email to Twitter employees, the billionaire owner said roughly half of the company’s revenue would need to come from subscriptions. But in the last few days, Twitter Blue, the premium tier for $7.99 a month that Musk has been pushing, has been through tumultuous changes in the short time it’s been live. As of writing, Twitter Blue has been suspended just days after the rushed launch — though who’s to say that won’t change in an hour.

articles.title: US debt hits $40 trillion: Who does Washington owe and why does it matter?
articles.summary: Heavy borrowing, increased spending and tax cuts by Democratic and Republican administrations have long raised concerns.
articles.body:
Total United States debt has surpassed $40 trillion for the first time in history, according to a Department of the Treasury update on Wednesday.

Ballooning debt, especially during President Donald Trump’s second term, which began in January last year, has raised concerns about a looming fiscal crisis for some time, with economists fearing a toxic combination of heavy borrowing, increased spending and lower taxes could land the world’s biggest economy in crisis.

The rising US debt comes despite Trump’s championing of cost-cutting and efficiency as a hallmark of his second term, with his Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) initiative slashing between 250,000 and 350,000 federal jobs and cutting global aid since the start of last year.

In May 2023, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) predicted that the US would reach the $40 trillion mark in 2028.

Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB), a budget watchdog, said in a statement, “$40 trillion of debt doesn’t exist solely on the government’s ledgers; it is felt throughout the economy and finds its way to the pocketbooks of people one way or another.”

Here’s what we know about why US debt is rising, and why it matters:

US debt is growing much faster in the 2020s than it did in previous decades.

Total debt, which includes debt owed to others and what the government owes itself, has doubled since January 2017, when Trump began his first term as president. US debt at the time was $19.95 trillion.

During Trump’s first term, public debt rose by $7.8 trillion, most of it because of the cost of the COVID-19 pandemic response. Since his return to office in January 2025, debt has grown by $3.8 trillion, bringing the total to $11.6 trillion across his two terms so far.

Under Joe Biden’s administration from 2021 to 2025, the government continued to borrow and spend heavily in response to the pandemic; debt rose by $8.4 trillion.

US debt hit $39 trillion in March this year, meaning it took fewer than five months to pile on an additional $1 trillion in debt.

By comparison, it took close to 200 years for total US debt to cross $1 trillion for the first time in 1981, according to an analysis by CRFB, although $1 trillion in 1981 would be worth $3.67 trillion in real terms today, after inflation is taken into account.

The CBO estimates that debt will rise from 101 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026 to 120 percent in 2036. That is well above the previous US record of 106 percent after World War II.

The soaring US debt “is an inevitable result of our demands for endless tax cuts, benefit expansions, and defence investments, and our refusal to address escalating Social Security and Medicare shortfalls,” Jessica Riedl, a budget and tax fellow at the Brookings Institution think tank, told Al Jazeera.

“We can blame politicians, but very few voters will back up their deficit concerns with a willingness to personally accept new taxes or benefit reductions. Sacrifice is reserved for our political opponents.”

Here are some of the specific factors that experts say have contributed to the fast-rising US debt.

There have been two major crises in nearly two decades, during which governments have needed to borrow and increase spending.

The 2007-09 recession was the first crisis, while the second was the 2020-23 COVID-19 pandemic, which is linked to about one-third of the debt run up since 2017, as borrowing under both the Trump and Biden presidencies intensified.

Analysts say another reason for rising borrowing is that tax and other revenues are not keeping up with spending, especially as the US is spending more to fund pensions and healthcare for an ageing population.

Experts say Democratic and Republican administrations alike have failed to rein in spending or raise taxes to close this gap.

The US spends about $7 trillion annually, with about 60 percent of that going to Social Security Administration (SSA) payments, health insurance including Medicare and Medicaid, and veterans’ care.

Revenues are inadequate to meet these expenses. For example, in July, the US brought in $334bn in individual income taxes, social insurance, corporate taxes and others, according to the Treasury Department.

However, it paid out $766bn, almost double the revenue, in social security, health insurance, national defence and interest payments.

Interest rates remained low until the pandemic hit, at which point the Federal Reserve raised rates to fight inflation.

Now, the US is paying about $1.1 trillion annually to service its debt, slightly more than it spends on defence. In the first 10 months of the 2026 budget year, interest costs have also eclipsed health insurance spending and are now the second-largest slice of spending after pensions. The US spends between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion per year on federal retirement benefits – Social Security – and state or local public pensions combined, according to data from analysis group USA Facts.

Despite these rising costs, Trump has implemented deep tax cuts for businesses, starting with his Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 during his first term, which slashed the corporate tax rate from 35 percent to 21 percent.

He followed that up in 2025 with his “One Beautiful Bill Act”, permanently entrenching the 2017 law. Although the bill also cut Medicaid spending by 12 percent, it raised the debt ceiling by nearly $5 trillion to allow for this.

At present, individual income taxes make up roughly half of federal revenues, compared with only 9 percent from corporate income taxes.

In between the two Trump presidencies, the Biden administration also spent heavily on infrastructure investment and clean energy subsidies.

Public debt borrowed from domestic and foreign investors makes up 80 percent – roughly $32 trillion – of the gross debt, according to Treasury data.

About $21 trillion of this public debt is owed domestically, to a variety of creditors including the Federal Reserve ($4.528 trillion), which buys and sells Treasury securities to influence federal interest rates and manage the money supply, according to analysis by the Peter G Peterson Foundation.

Other creditors are mutual funds ($5.195 trillion), pension funds ($1.135 trillion), state and local governments ($1.636 trillion), commercial banks and depository institutions ($2.083 trillion) and other corporate and individual lenders ($6.660 trillion).

Internationally, the US is in debt to several countries and private investors. In 1970, total foreign debt holders accounted for 5 percent of gross debt, but by 2025, they made up 32 percent. That means while they are helping boost US economic activity, more of the country’s income is being sent abroad in the form of interest payments.

By 2025, the US owed Japan $1.203 trillion, the United Kingdom ($889bn), China ($683bn), as well as owing more than 30 other entities.

Separately, another 20 percent of the gross national debt – about $8 trillion – is owed intra-governmentally and therefore does not affect overall finances.

What does rising debt mean for the US economy?

Analysts say the rising debt could potentially create an economic crisis for the US, in the form of hyperinflation or higher interest rates, for example, if it goes unchecked.

As more debt piles on, there is a growing risk that private investment will fall because of safety concerns, and as a consequence, economic growth could slow down.

“We’re already paying the cost. This debt is slowing growth, pushing up interest rates, and worsening inflation,” Riedl of Brookings said.

In 2026, the US is expected to spend 19 percent of federal tax revenues on interest payments. That share is expected to rise to 20 percent in a decade and 50 percent in three decades, “even under the rosiest scenarios,” she added. “The longer we wait to make the difficult fiscal decisions, the more painful and drastic those reforms will be.”

Lawmakers may eventually be forced to respond with painful austerity measures such as higher taxes, analysts say. Social safety net programmes could also be at risk.

It could take years to resolve, experts warn, and the consequences could be intergenerational, with young people forced to pay more for many years.

The rest of the world would be affected too: the US is a cornerstone of the global economy, and a crisis there will likely hurt global markets.

The first correcting step, MacGuineas of CRFB said, is to commit to zero new borrowing immediately. Lawmakers must also set up a bipartisan fiscal commission to scrutinise the issues, she said. With a commitment to keep taxes low and reduce spending, while also engaging in a hugely expensive war in the Middle East, this may be difficult to achieve, analysts say.

articles.title: Dólar abre em queda com pesquisas eleitorais e fim da escala 6x1 no radar | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 1,17%, cotada a R$ 5,0871. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 1,06%, aos 204.324 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 1,17%, cotada a R$ 5,0871. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 1,06%, aos 204.324 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar abriu esta sexta-feira (16) em queda de 0,08% , cotado a R$ 5,0832 , por volta das 9h08. Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, começa a ser negociado às 10h.

▶️Após ser aprovada pelo Senado, a proposta que prevê mudanças na escala de trabalho 6x1 será promulgada pela Mesa do Congresso Nacional em sessão solene nesta sexta-feira. A medida faz parte de uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC), que altera a Constituição Federal.

▶️ No quadro eleitoral, as duas pesquisas presidenciais mais recentes , divulgadas pelo Datafolha e pela Quaest, mostram um cenário de empate técnico entre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Lula (PT) na disputa pelo segundo turno das eleições de 2026. Acompanhe as pesquisas eleitorais no g1.

▶️Também repercute a entrevista do presidente Lula na TV Globo na quinta-feira (15). Nesta sexta-feira (16), será a vez do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ser entrevistado.

▶️ Na agenda econômica, o destaque é a divulgação do Índice de Atividade Econômica (IBC-Br) de agosto pelo Banco Central do Brasil (BC) , prevista para as 9h. Em julho, o indicador recuou 0,22% ante junho, na série com ajuste sazonal, mas avançou 1,1% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025.

🔎 O IBC-Br é um indicador do Banco Central que funciona como uma espécie de termômetro da atividade econômica do Brasil. Ele ajuda a avaliar se a economia está crescendo ou perdendo força.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Datafolha e Quaest mostram empate técnico entre Lula e Flávio

As pesquisas mais recentes do Datafolha e da Quaest mostram empate técnico entre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Lula (PT) na disputa pelo segundo turno das eleições de 2026.

Embora o senador apareça numericamente à frente nos dois levantamentos, a diferença está dentro da margem de erro, de dois pontos percentuais. As duas pesquisas têm nível de confiança de 95%.

▶️ Datafolha : divulgado na quinta-feira, o levantamento aponta Flávio com 47% das intenções de voto, ante 45% de Lula . Na semana anterior, o senador tinha 49%, enquanto o presidente mantinha 45%, reduzindo a diferença de quatro para dois pontos percentuais.

▶️ Quaest: publicado na quarta-feira (14), o levantamento mostra Flávio com 46% e Lula com 44% . Outros 9% pretendem votar em branco, anular o voto ou não comparecer às urnas; 1% está indeciso.

Na entrevista à TV Globo na noite de ontem, Lula defendeu reduzir a maioridade penal em casos de crimes hediondos, pediu a investigação de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) citados em suspeitas envolvendo Daniel Vorcaro e comentou a relação comercial com os Estados Unidos .

Conduzida por Renata Lo Prete, a entrevista foi transmitida pela TV Globo, GloboNews e g1.

Nesta sexta-feira, será a vez de Flávio Bolsonaro ser entrevistado por Renata Lo Prete, como parte da cobertura do segundo turno das Eleições 2026. Veja quando e onde assistir .

A Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê o fim da escala 6x1, com dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana, foi aprovada pelo Senado nesta quarta-feira (14).

A proposta foi aprovada por 75 votos a favor e um contra nos dois turnos de votação. O senador Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS) foi o único a votar contrário à proposta.

Com a aprovação, a emenda constitucional é promulgada pela Mesa do Congresso, sem precisar passar pela sanção do presidente da República, como ocorre com projetos de lei. Ela começa a produzir efeitos após a publicação no Diário Oficial.

Como o g1 mostrou , a expectativa é que as mudanças comecem a valer dois meses após a publicação da emenda constitucional. A partir desse prazo, os trabalhadores passariam a ter direito a dois dias de repouso semanal remunerado, com possibilidade de compensação prevista em norma coletiva, desde que fosse assegurada a média de dois dias de descanso por semana.

A proposta também prevê a redução gradual da jornada semanal, sem diminuição salarial. Durante o primeiro ano de transição, o limite será de 42 horas semanais. Depois desse período, a jornada máxima passará a ser de 40 horas.

A atividade econômica brasileira cresceu 0,3% em agosto, após registrar queda de 0,3% em julho, segundo dados divulgados pelo Banco Central. Foi a primeira alta em três meses.

O resultado foi puxado pela indústria, que avançou 0,9%, e pelos serviços, com crescimento de 0,2%. Já a agropecuária recuou 1,8%.

Na comparação com agosto de 2025, a atividade econômica cresceu 1,2%. No acumulado de janeiro a agosto e em 12 meses, a alta foi de 1,6%.

Os dados são do Índice de Atividade Econômica do Banco Central (IBC-Br), indicador que funciona como um termômetro da economia e ajuda a antecipar tendências do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

🔎 O desempenho da economia também é acompanhado pelo Banco Central na definição da taxa básica de juros. Quando a atividade está aquecida, a demanda por produtos e serviços pode aumentar e pressionar a inflação, o que dificulta a redução dos juros.

Em Wall Street , os contratos futuros das bolsas tinham desempenho misto nesta sexta-feira (16), com investidores preocupados com os altos gastos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA) e o endividamento de empresas que operam centros de processamento de dados.

No pré-mercado, as ações da Tesla subiam 4,4%, enquanto empresas ligadas à infraestrutura de IA, como CoreWeave e Nebius, registravam perdas.

Os investidores também acompanham as perspectivas para os juros americanos. O mercado espera que o Federal Reserve ( Fed ), banco central dos EUA, mantenha as taxas inalteradas neste mês.

🛢️ Já o petróleo recuava quase 1%, mas o barril do Brent continuava acima de US$ 100.

Na Ásia , as bolsas fecharam em alta, recuperando parte das perdas da sessão anterior, em meio a sinais de apoio do governo chinês e anúncios de resultados financeiros de empresas de IA.

Apesar da recuperação, o índice CSI300, que reúne grandes empresas chinesas, caiu 3,4% na semana, o pior resultado em três meses.

Em Tóquio, o Nikkei subiu 1,39%, enquanto o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, avançou 0,52%. Em Seul , o Kospi teve alta de 2,05%. Xangai ganhou 0,24%, e o CSI300 avançou 0,11%.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters.

articles.title: Trabalho Infantil ai 9,2% e Atinge Menor Nível da Série Histórica | G1
articles.standfirst: Número de crianças e adolescentes nessa situação recuou 9,2% em 2025, segundo o IBGE. Apesar da melhora, 525 mil ainda exerciam atividades consideradas entre as piores formas de trabalho infantil, com riscos à saúde e à segurança.
articles.summary: Número de crianças e adolescentes nessa situação recuou 9,2% em 2025, segundo o IBGE. Apesar da melhora, 525 mil ainda exerciam atividades consideradas entre as piores formas de trabalho infantil, com riscos à saúde e à segurança.
articles.body:
O número de crianças e adolescentes de 5 a 17 anos em situação de trabalho infantil no Brasil caiu para 1,499 milhão em 2025, uma redução de 9,2% em relação ao ano anterior.

São o menor número e a menor proporção já registrados pela Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua), do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), desde o início da série histórica, em 2016.

Naquele ano, o país tinha 2,1 milhões de crianças e adolescentes nessa situação, o equivalente a 5,2% da população dessa faixa etária. Em 2025, a proporção recuou para 4% .

Isso representa cerca de 151 mil crianças e adolescentes a menos no trabalho infantil.

Gráfico de trabalho infantil no Brasil — Foto: g1

A queda não significa que o problema esteja resolvido. Mais de um terço dos que realizavam atividades econômicas, cerca de 525 mil pessoas, trabalhava nas chamadas piores formas de trabalho infantil , que envolvem atividades capazes de comprometer a saúde, a segurança e o desenvolvimento.

🔍 O IBGE considera em situação de trabalho infantil crianças e adolescentes de 5 a 17 anos que realizam atividades econômicas ou produzem bens para o próprio consumo, conforme os critérios da pesquisa. A legislação brasileira proíbe qualquer trabalho antes dos 14 anos e permite a aprendizagem a partir dessa idade. Aos 16 e 17 anos, o trabalho é permitido, mas há restrições.

Cerca de 525 mil crianças e adolescentes estavam ocupados nas chamadas piores formas de trabalho infantil, o equivalente a 36,2% daqueles que realizavam atividades econômicas. É o menor número da série histórica.

🔍 A classificação segue a Lista das Piores Formas de Trabalho Infantil (Lista TIP) , prevista no Decreto nº 6.481, de 2008. Ela inclui atividades que podem colocar em risco a saúde, a segurança e a moralidade de crianças e adolescentes, como determinados trabalhos com máquinas perigosas, produtos químicos e em condições insalubres.

Na comparação com 2024, quando a estimativa era de 560 mil pessoas, houve queda de 6,3%. Em relação a 2016, quando 919 mil crianças e adolescentes estavam nessas ocupações, a redução acumulada chega a 42,9%.

O perfil desse grupo também revela desigualdades: 72,6% eram meninos e 68,3% eram pretos ou pardos. Além disso, 333 mil tinham entre 16 e 17 anos, o equivalente a mais de 60% dos que estavam nas piores formas de trabalho infantil.

Adolescentes de 16 e 17 anos concentram a maioria dos casos

O trabalho infantil é mais frequente entre os mais velhos. Em 2025, os adolescentes de 16 e 17 anos correspondiam a 58,1% do total de crianças e adolescentes nessa situação: eram 871 mil pessoas, ou 14,5% da população dessa faixa etária.

Entre os jovens de 14 e 15 anos , havia 348 mil pessoas em situação de trabalho infantil, o equivalente a 5,9% da população dessa faixa etária. Já entre crianças de 5 a 13 anos , eram 280 mil casos, ou 1,1% do total nessa idade.

Nesse último grupo, 190 mil crianças, ou 67,7% do total, estavam envolvidas exclusivamente em atividades voltadas ao próprio consumo, como a produção de alimentos para a família.

O levantamento também mostra desigualdades por sexo e raça ou cor. Os meninos representavam 65,4% das crianças e adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil, enquanto as meninas correspondiam a 34,6% . Crianças e adolescentes pretos ou pardos somavam 67% do total .

⚠️ Nem todo adolescente que trabalha está necessariamente em situação irregular. A classificação como trabalho infantil depende da idade, da atividade exercida e das condições de trabalho, conforme os critérios da legislação e da pesquisa.

A legislação brasileira estabelece regras diferentes para cada idade:

Até os 13 anos, qualquer trabalho é proibido.

Aos 14 e 15 anos, é permitido apenas o trabalho na condição de aprendiz.

A partir dos 16 anos, o trabalho é autorizado, mas há restrições: menores de 18 anos não podem exercer atividades noturnas, perigosas ou insalubres, nem ocupações incluídas na Lista TIP.

Entre os adolescentes de 16 e 17 anos que trabalhavam, 67% estavam na informalidade, o equivalente a aproximadamente 705 mil pessoas. O percentual foi o menor da série histórica. Em 2022, a taxa era de 76,3% .

A relação entre trabalho e educação é outro ponto de atenção. Entre as crianças e os adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil, a taxa de escolarização era de 86,9% , abaixo dos 97,5% registrados entre todas as crianças e adolescentes de 5 a 17 anos.

A diferença é ainda maior entre os jovens de 16 e 17 anos. Nessa faixa, 79,6% daqueles em situação de trabalho infantil frequentavam a escola, ante 89,6% do total de adolescentes da mesma idade.

A diferença de 10 pontos percentuais não significa, por si só, que o trabalho tenha provocado o abandono escolar em todos os casos, mas mostra que os adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil têm menor frequência escolar.

Os dados de rendimento também mostram diferenças entre os grupos. Crianças e adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil recebiam, em média, R$ 936 por mês. Entre os que ainda estudavam, o rendimento médio era de R$ 844 , enquanto aqueles que haviam deixado a escola recebiam R$ 1.326 .

A diferença é compatível com a possibilidade de jornadas mais longas entre os jovens que não frequentam a escola.

Sudeste tem mais casos; Norte, maior proporção

A distribuição regional mostra que o Sudeste concentrava o maior número de crianças e adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil, com 481 mil pessoas.

O Nordeste vinha em seguida, com 408 mil, seguido pelo Norte , com 249 mil, pelo Sul , com 233 mil, e pelo Centro-Oeste, com 128 mil.

🙍‍♂️ Quando o cálculo considera a proporção de crianças e adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil em relação à população de cada região, porém, o cenário muda. O Norte apresentava a maior taxa do país, de 6,3%, enquanto o Sudeste registrava a menor, de 3,3%.

Isso significa que, embora o Sudeste concentre mais casos em números absolutos, o trabalho infantil representa uma parcela maior da população jovem no Norte.

O Nordeste, por sua vez, teve a maior redução acumulada entre 2016 e 2025, de 45,6%. Na comparação entre 2022 e 2025, a queda na região foi de 29,2%.

Bolsa Família concentra mais de 95% da redução em 2025

A redução do trabalho infantil ocorreu principalmente entre crianças e adolescentes que vivem em famílias beneficiárias do Bolsa Família . De 2024 para 2025, o número de jovens em situação de trabalho infantil nessas famílias caiu 20,1% , de acordo com os dados da PNAD Contínua.

Isso representa 144 mil crianças e adolescentes a menos nesse grupo, o equivalente a mais de 95% da redução de 151 mil casos registrada no país no período.

Em 2025, 573 mil crianças e adolescentes de 5 a 17 anos que viviam em famílias atendidas pelo programa estavam em situação de trabalho infantil. O número corresponde a 4,4% das crianças e adolescentes que vivem nessas famílias.

Ao todo, 13,1 milhões de crianças e adolescentes nessa faixa etária moravam em famílias beneficiárias do Bolsa Família, o equivalente a 34,7% da população de 5 a 17 anos no país.

A diferença de renda entre os domicílios também chama a atenção. A renda média mensal por pessoa era de R$ 660 nas famílias beneficiárias, contra R$ 1.990 naquelas que não recebiam o benefício.

Os números mostram que a redução do trabalho infantil esteve fortemente concentrada entre as famílias atendidas pelo programa.

A comparação, porém, não permite atribuir toda a queda exclusivamente ao Bolsa Família: outros fatores econômicos e sociais também podem influenciar a entrada de crianças e adolescentes no mercado de trabalho antes da idade permitida.

Fiscalização bate recorde, mas problema é grande

Enquanto o IBGE estima a dimensão do trabalho infantil no país por meio de uma pesquisa domiciliar, a fiscalização federal atua para identificar casos de trabalho infantil e afastar crianças e adolescentes de atividades ilegais.

Minas Gerais, com 830 afastamentos, e São Paulo, com 629, registraram os maiores números entre os estados. Esses números são bem menores que o total de 1,499 milhão de crianças e adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil estimado pelo IBGE para o mesmo ano.

A comparação ajuda a mostrar a diferença entre o total estimado pela pesquisa e os casos identificados pela fiscalização, mas não representa uma taxa de cobertura oficial: os dois indicadores são produzidos por métodos diferentes, e as fiscalizações podem se concentrar em situações de maior gravidade.

As dificuldades para enfrentar o problema incluem a informalidade, a existência de locais de trabalho espalhados pelo país e a dificuldade de identificar situações que ocorrem em ambientes privados, como o trabalho doméstico. A atuação dos auditores-fiscais também depende da estrutura disponível para realizar fiscalizações em todo o país.

Além das ações de fiscalização, o número de denúncias também aumentou em 2025. O Disque 100 recebeu cerca de 5,1 mil denúncias relacionadas ao trabalho infantil, alta de 19,4% em relação ao ano anterior. articles.title: No 1º aumento em três meses, 'prévia do PIB' do Banco Central registra alta de 0,3% em agosto | G1
articles.standfirst: Números mostram que a indústria e os serviços puxaram o crescimento da atividade em agosto. Na parcial do ano e em doze meses até agosto, indicador avançou 1,6%.
articles.summary: Números mostram que a indústria e os serviços puxaram o crescimento da atividade em agosto. Na parcial do ano e em doze meses até agosto, indicador avançou 1,6%.
articles.body:
O Índice de Atividade Econômica (IBC-Br), divulgado pelo Banco Central do Brasil (BC) nesta sexta-feira (16), mostrou expansão de 0,3% em agosto, na comparação com o mês anterior.

Esse foi o primeiro aumento do IBC-Br, do Banco Central, em três meses.

🔎 O cálculo é feito após ajuste sazonal — ou seja, uma forma de comparar períodos diferentes.

O resultado representa melhora em relação a julho, quando houve contração de 0,3% no indicador.

Ainda segundo o Banco Central, o IBC-Br apresentou crescimento de 1,2% na comparação com o mesmo mês do ano passado.

Na parcial do ano, o indicador avançou 1,6% e, em 12 meses até agosto, teve aumento também de 1,6%. Nesses casos, o índice foi calculado sem ajuste sazonal.

Veja abaixo o desempenho setor por setor em agosto:

➡️O PIB é a soma de todos os bens e serviços produzidos no país e serve para medir a evolução da economia. O resultado oficial, medido pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), tem uma metodologia diferente (veja mais abaixo nessa reportagem).

🔎Se o PIB cresce, significa que a economia vai bem e produz mais. Se o PIB cai, quer dizer que a economia está encolhendo. Entretanto, nem sempre crescimento do PIB equivale a bem estar social.

Em um ano eleitoral, o governo tem adotado ações para estimular a economia e reduzir o endividamento da população, o que impulsiona a demanda por produtos e serviços .

A equipe econômica zerou, por exemplo, a tributação do imposto de renda para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil , além de ter liberado o Fundo de Garantia por Tempo de Serviço (FGTS) e linhas de crédito mais baratas para a população.

A estratégia do governo, porém, dificulta o controle da inflação. O BC tem dito claramente que uma desaceleração, ou seja, um ritmo menor de crescimento da economia, faz parte da estratégia de conter as pressões inflacionárias.

▶️Na ata da última reunião do Copom, divulgada em setembro, o BC informou que o chamado "hiato do produto" segue positivo.

Isso quer dizer que a economia continua operando acima do seu potencial de crescimento sem pressionar a inflação.

O mercado financeiro acredita em desaceleração da economia no ano de 2026 fechado. A projeção dos analistas é de uma expansão de cerca de 1,85% em 2026, contra um crescimento de 2,3% no ano passado.

Fachada do Banco Central, em Brasília — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Os resultados do IBC-Br são considerados a "prévia do PIB". Porém, o cálculo do Banco Central é diferente do cálculo do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

O indicador do BC incorpora estimativas para a agropecuária, a indústria e o setor de serviços, além dos impostos, mas não considera o lado da demanda (incorporado no cálculo do PIB do IBGE).

O IBC-Br é uma das ferramentas usadas pelo BC para definir a taxa básica de juros do país. Com o maior crescimento da economia, por exemplo, teoricamente haveria mais pressão inflacionária, o que poderia contribuir para conter a queda dos juros.

articles.title: Online festive sales: Lower AOVs, bigger share of purchases through EMIs
articles.summary: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales are somewhat missing the fiery spark this year.
articles.body: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales are somewhat missing the fiery spark this year. Price hikes have weighed on smartphone sales volumes, typically the biggest driver of the season with final prices in many cases higher than last year even after discounts. Price increases have also made durables costlier with the share of large-ticket purchases (overall) through EMIs having significantly gone up this year—on Amazon, for instance, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year, said Aman Deep Lohan, director, home, kitchen and outdoors at Amazon India. Amid inflation shrinking household budgets, smaller-ticket items found more space in shopping carts with consumers prioritising value for money. At the end of a week’s sales, average order values (AOV) are lower with growth having been led by categories such as fashion, beauty, home and general merchandise.“Value commerce, which covers items priced below Rs 500, handled about half of all festive orders. AOVs are 7-8% lower than last year because the basket moved to lower-ticket categories and channels. By value, phones and electronics still lead; by growth, softlines lead,” said Nikhil Dalal, associate partner, Redseer Strategy Consultants, which captured data from Oct 8-12. On Flipkart, about 7 in 10 units sold were priced under Rs 500.Unlike other seasons when a major chunk of the sales happen during Navaratri (the first leg of sale), analysts expect sales this year to be more spread out through Diwali as consumers strike a balance between their pockets and desire to buy. Estimates from Datum Intelligence showed that sales dropped by about 7-10% in the first four opening days to Rs 29,800-30,900 crore. “Last year’s sales opened on Sept 22, the day the GST rate cuts took effect. This year’s opening had no such trigger,” analysts at the firm said.Shrinking discounts, bigger EMIsAs price hikes shrunk the quantum of discounts on offer, particularly in demand-heavy categories such as smartphones, consumers went bigger on EMIs to buy premium products. “Phones entered the sale with average prices about 15% higher than a year ago. so even a similar headline discount leaves the final price above last year’s festive price. Across devices, sale-day prices were only about 5% to 10% below pre-sale levels, depending on category. Discounts were deeper where inventory and competition allowed: smartwatches and smart rings about 10%-15% below pre-sale prices, and some budget phones 10-15%,” Dalal said. Consumers opted for EMIs to buy 55-inch television sets, premium laptops and make other upgrades, said Lohan. Flipkart has also enabled cross-category exchanges—for instance, an old laptop can be traded for a new phone. “EMIs and bank offers saw increased adoption, signifying how customers are leveraging affordability options for their purchases this festive season,” said a Myntra spokesperson.Small town shoppers lead the festive queueWith the coverage of the internet and smartphones expanding, more small town consumers are taking to online shopping. What also helps is the wider availability of brands on e-commerce platforms. On Flipkart, consumers from places such as Sardulgarh, Panskura and Kishanganj logged in, making up some of the fastest-growing markets at the opening of the sale. About 60-65% of orders on Amazon came from tier 2 and 3 markets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Fairfax does not cut jobs, more avenues likely: Prem Watsa
articles.summary: India-born Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, whose group Fairfax won the bid to buy 60.7% in IDBI Bank, is upbeat about India and its prospects.
articles.body: India-born Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, whose group Fairfax won the bid to buy 60.7% in IDBI Bank, is upbeat about India and its prospects. He discusses the way forward for the bank and synergies with Go Digit and IIFL. Excerpts:It’s been a long wait since the process started. How do you view the acquisition and how will it fit into your overall scheme of things?This is the biggest acquisition we’ve ever made. This is because we think India is the place to be, the Indian economy is going to do really well with the goal of Viksit Bharat and $30 trillion by 2047. The next two decades are going to be huge for India, particularly with the fact that you’ve got free trade (pacts). The Prime Minister and Piyush Goyal are negotiating deals with so many countries. This means you can make in India and sell it to the world. India has got great people, the engineers are so good. You have so many Indian CEOs leading global corporations. There’s going to be massive money flowing into India, from the US, Canada, Europe, Japan, from all over the world. There’s going to be a glorious time for everybody with huge employment. The banking system will benefit. China had a period like that from 2000 to 2010, with 10-11% real growth. India is at that level. Now, the focus will be on India.What are your plans for IDBI Bank?We’ve got property insurance, life insurance through Go Digit, which is going there (to IDBI). Wealth management and investment banking, which are with IIFL, are also going there. You’ve got a very powerful combination there with focus on customers and on providing outstanding service. We can attract pretty much anyone to join IDBI Bank. Rakesh (Sharma) is going to build that. It has 2,000 branches but it hasn’t expanded a lot due to the challenges it faced. All that has been dealt with.What will be your message to employees, some of whom are unsure about the future?Over 40 years, Fairfax has treated employees better than almost any company you can think of. We follow the golden rule which is to treat people like you want to be treated yourself. We have never laid off 5% or 10% of the staff. We’re going to work with them and we’re going to have this huge growth opportunity, which means you need people. The service conditions and their other benefits will, of course, remain. When Covid came, we never changed any benefits, we never changed any bonuses, not one person was let go of during that time.You have announced plans for Go Digit, IIFL Capital Services today. Will the exercise also involve restructuring of some of the IDBI subsidiaries and what is the road map for CSB Bank?We have got two years. So, we are going to look at that carefully, as soon as we close (the IDBI transaction). But we see insurance opportunities for banking clients and banking opportunities for insurance clients and the same for IIFL Capital. We have very good people, we believe in decentralised operations but working together. That’s how Fairfax was built. We see that taking place in IDBI Bank over time.Will you have a holding company structure, you have life, general insurance and reinsurance?Go Digit will be independent. It’ll have a board and will be independently run by Kamesh (Goyal). IIFL will be run by Venkat, Vasu and Nirmal. We weren’t going to change the structure in any way: no change in IIFL Capital, no change in Go Digit.The RBI mandate is to reduce your holding in IDBI to 40% in 10 years and to 26% in 15 years. What will be the dilution plan?We are focused on building the bank. Also, remember that when we began the insurance business it was 26% (FDI cap), which increased to 49% then to 74% and now it’s at 100%. We’ll see what happens in the future. We will go by whatever the regulations are at that point of time.Given the large diaspora in Canada, do you want to use the Canada-India corridor and have some IDBI branches there?No. My focus will be on India first. It has such a big market, 1.5 billion people. There are around 300 million people in the middle class, which is likely to double in 10 years. The US population is around 350 million. So, you go from 300 to 600 million, and there is going to be so much demand for all the services: the accounts, insurance. If you look at Singapore, when Lee Kuan Yew was first elected, apart from real estate, banking was the best investment option, it compounded 20% for the longest time. Once an economy is a developed economy, it doesn’t grow like that. It’s unbelievable how banking is needed. It’s the lifeline for any economy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Irdai looking at ways to help policyholders stay the course
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Irdai is exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values to help policyholders avoid premature surrenders and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Irdai is exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values to help policyholders avoid premature surrenders and retain policies until maturity, chairman Ajay Seth said at Samvaad 2026, organised by Sahamati, the self-regulatory organisation for account aggregators.Many policyholders surrender policies when they need money or face a temporary income shortfall, particularly those outside the salaried workforce. Financing the final few premium instalments could help them retain the policy and realise better value at maturity, while giving lenders an existing policy value as security. "A significant number of policyholders surrender their policies because they need money. Another situation arises when income varies, particularly among people who are not salaried," Seth said. "Financing those final instalments could be useful. If the premiums are paid over time, the policyholder can realise better value, while the lender has an embedded value to rely on."Seth said a grey market had emerged for policy assignments, which he said were not permitted under the Insurance Act. articles.title: CERT-In issues 'critical' alert as AI agents access 'confidential' data of Indian firms'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a “critical” alert after autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents under test accessed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a “critical” alert after autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents under test accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations without authorisation.The agency has also warned that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster, leaving businesses with only hours to respond.In an advisory titled AI Agents as Attack Vectors, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) detailed two types of incidents affecting the country's organisations.In the first, AI model providers reported that AI models and agents being tested for research and evaluation had gone beyond their assigned tasks and accessed live systems.The agents were able to read business records containing personal information and confidential material by using credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and cloud services with excessive access permissions.A key concern was that none of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access themselves. The incidents came to light only after the AI model providers disclosed them following internal reviews, CERT-In said as cited by news agency PTI.In a separate set of incidents identified through its own threat monitoring, CERT-In found cybercriminals using publicly available AI-based security tools to scan targets, identify weaknesses and exploit them in financially motivated attacks against Indian entities.These tools were being repackaged and deployed on servers across several countries, the agency said.ALSO READ: Perched in Sikkim, India’s first digital nomad village logs in to local lifeAI tools speed up cyberattacksAccording to CERT-In, the use of AI-powered tools reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage from several days to just a few hours. Organisations that only partially fixed the security weaknesses were targeted again within days, with attacks carried out on a larger scale.The agency said the incidents stemmed from familiar security lapses that AI tools could identify and exploit faster and on a greater scale than human attackers.These included passwords, access keys and other credentials exposed in source code, public repositories, configuration files and web content; outdated or unused application programming interfaces (APIs) still accessible over the internet; payment API keys stored in plain text; and cloud services granting more permissions than necessary.Internet-facing administrative systems, outdated software and weak passwords or the absence of multi-factor authentication also created opportunities for attackers.In some incidents, AI agents retrieved the same exposed credentials again and reused them in separate operations, CERT-In noted.What organisations should doCERT-In has urged organisations to audit their source code, public repositories and their histories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage to identify exposed credentials. Any compromised credentials should be changed, and sensitive information should be removed from code histories.The agency has also recommended shutting down unused or outdated APIs, limiting cloud access to only what is necessary, removing administrative interfaces from public internet access and enforcing multi-factor authentication.Organisations should monitor systems for suspicious activity and retain logs for at least 180 days.You use AI every day. The blockbuster gains came after the IT firm reported a 32.74% jump in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.Tech Mahindra, along with other IT stocks helped domestic equity benchmarks shake off a sluggish start.Around 12.30 pm, Tech Mahindra shares were trading 8.05% higher at Rs 1,781.50 on the BSE. Following the rise, Tech Mahindra's market capitalisation increased by Rs 10,974.86 crore to Rs 1,72,895.16 crore.The company's consolidated net profit attributable to its owners rose 32.74% year on year to Rs 1,585.6 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,194.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Compared with the preceding quarter, net profit increased 8%, while revenue rose 3%.Alongside its earnings announcement, Tech Mahindra's board recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:1 to mark the company's 40th anniversary. The proposal means shareholders will receive one additional share for every share they hold. The company said in a regulatory filing that the bonus shares are expected to be credited by December 15.The proposed issue will be the company's first in 11 years. Its previous bonus issue, also in the ratio of 1:1, was announced in March 2015.IT shares lift benchmarks, but oil prices remain a concernThe rally in technology stocks helped the domestic market turn positive after a muted start on Friday. articles.body: MUMBAI: SBI Card has launched the Eternal SBI Card with instant discounts across Zomato, Blinkit, District and Bistro, along with 5% cashback on spending at partner brands Apollo 24|7, ixigo, Uber and Urban Company.The co-branded credit card, launched in partnership with Eternal (formerly Zomato), will be available from October 22 in phases. Customers can request early access through the Zomato, Blinkit and District apps and receive an invitation to apply.The card offers 10% instant discounts on Zomato and District transactions, and on electronics and beauty purchases on Blinkit. Other eligible Blinkit purchases qualify for a 5% discount, while Bistro transactions attract a 10% discount. Discounts across these platforms are capped at Rs 2,000 a month and apply over and above existing platform offers.Cardholders also get 5% cashback on spending at Apollo 24|7, ixigo, Uber and Urban Company, capped at Rs 1,000 a month. Cashback is automatically credited to the SBI Card account when the statement is generated.The card offers a 1+1 movie ticket deal on District, with the discount on the second ticket capped at Rs 200. It carries a joining fee of Rs 499 and includes a complimentary six-month Zomato Gold membership. The annual fee of Rs 499 is waived if spending reaches Rs 2 lakh in the preceding year.The card also provides a 1% fuel surcharge waiver of up to Rs 200 per statement cycle. It will be available on the Mastercard and RuPay networks, with applications processed digitally through the Zomato, Blinkit and District apps.Salila Pande, managing director and CEO of SBI Card, said the launch would strengthen the company's retail co-branded credit card portfolio. Akshant Goyal, CFO of Eternal, said the card aims to offer greater value on frequent transactions across the group's platforms while extending benefits to spending outside its ecosystem.You use AI every day. articles.title: India could face inflation risks if Middle East conflict keeps energy prices on edge: IMF
articles.summary: India could face fresh inflationary pressures if the Middle East conflict keeps energy prices high for longer, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has
articles.body: India could face fresh inflationary pressures if the Middle East conflict keeps energy prices high for longer, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned. While India has kept its oil pipelines running by sourcing from alternative markets, the agency has predicted that prolonged high energy prices could raise costs, slow economic growth and increase the cost of living.The warning features in the IMF's October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook for Asia and the Pacific, which lists a prolonged Middle East conflict among the major downside risks facing the region. Although India and some other large Asian economies have adjusted their oil sourcing to limit the disruption, the report cautioned that sustained energy price pressures could prolong the economic impact of the conflict.The shift in supply sources has helped India, Japan and Korea bring oil flows back to the levels recorded before the conflict. The IMF attributed this recovery partly to the countries' ability to secure supplies from outside the Middle East.“For other large Asian economies (including India, Japan, and Korea), the resilience in part reflects adaptation by securing oil from alternative sources outside the Middle East,” the report said. It added that total oil flows to these countries had returned to their pre-conflict rates since June.Refined fuel prices add to cost pressuresThe pressure on energy costs has not been uniform across products. The IMF noted that refined petroleum products, particularly diesel and jet fuel, had recorded sharper price increases than crude oil following the conflict.If these costs remain high, businesses could face increased transportation and production expenses, with the impact potentially extending to consumers. The report warned that a prolonged conflict could keep energy prices elevated and sustain wider commodity price pressures.“A prolonged conflict in the Middle East could sustain high energy prices,” the IMF said, describing persistent energy disruptions as a key downside risk for the Asia-Pacific region.Higher energy bills pose a fiscal challengeExpensive energy could also leave governments across the region with less room to manage their finances while providing relief to households facing higher costs. The IMF warned that rising energy prices could worsen fiscal balances, making it harder to protect vulnerable sections of the population without undermining fiscal sustainability.The report recommended that governments focus on targeted assistance rather than measures that apply broadly across the economy. “Fiscal policy should prioritize preserving sustainability while protecting vulnerable households,” it said, advocating targeted and time-bound support instead of broad-based fuel subsidies or price controls.AI investments and global financial conditions among other risksThe IMF also pointed to uncertainty over artificial intelligence investments and tighter global financial conditions as potential sources of pressure on regional growth.A correction in AI-related investments or asset valuations could weigh on business investment and private consumption. Separately, higher global sovereign yields could spill over into regional bond markets, adding to the challenges facing Asian economies.The IMF has projected India's GDP growth at 7% in 2026 and 2027, with private consumption and services activity expected to support expansion. However, managing external shocks and maintaining macroeconomic stability will remain important to sustaining this growth.To strengthen the region's ability to withstand future disruptions, the IMF called for improvements in energy security, investment in digital infrastructure and skills, and policies focused on price stability.You use AI every day. articles.title: US-based homebuyer paid Rs 15 lakh for Rs 10.41 lakh flat, but builder demanded Rs 20 lakh more and allegedly threatened him; commission orders refund with 12% interest and Rs 10 lakh compensation
articles.summary: Buying a home and getting its possession can be two different things, and in many cases the latter is delayed, causing grievance to the homebuyer.
articles.body: Buying a home and getting its possession can be two different things, and in many cases the latter is delayed, causing grievance to the homebuyer. In one such case, a man based in the US bought a house in India but the possession of the flat was repeatedly delayed, prompting a legal fight.The homebuyer also ended up paying much more than the initial amount decided for the flat, and finally got relief with the consumer commission. Let’s read on to know what happened:What the case is aboutA man, who was working in the US, booked a 1,208-square-foot flat along with a car parking space in Patna. The booking was confirmed in 2005, and the agreement for sale was signed in 2007.The total price agreed upon for the flat and parking space was Rs 10,41,250. Before the agreement was executed, the man had already paid Rs 9 lakh to the builder. He also paid Rs 2 lakh as commission to a partner in the construction company.Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additionsThe outstanding amount of Rs 1,41,250 was scheduled to be paid in two installments, due in 2007, and 2008. The possession was expected by August 2008. However, the man kept waiting for several years for the flat and eventually decided to take the builder and the company to court in 2012.He initially filed a complaint that year, but it was dismissed in 2017. In 2019, he approached the National Commission, which sent the matter back to the State Commission for consideration. The present case was heard by the State Commission following that remand, according to an ET report.Builder demands additional paymentEven before the scheduled handover, the man was asked to pay an additional Rs 4 lakh into the account of the construction company's partner on the grounds that “the construction cost has gone up”. Although he objected to the demand, he eventually paid the amount through two cheques in 2007.Despite paying more than the agreed price, the man still did not get possession of the flat. His mother subsequently visited the builder's office to find out why the property had not been handed over. During the visit, the builder and the company's partner demanded another Rs 2 lakh as the final payment before giving possession of the flat and parking space.Also Read | He bought a home, gave it for redevelopment years later and sold new flat for Rs 1.95 crore within 8 days; taxman denied LTCG exemption and added Rs 80.14 lakh, but ITAT grants reliefThe man paid this additional amount by cheque in 2008. His total payments to the builder thus reached Rs 13 lakh against the original consideration of Rs 10.41 lakh. This amount was over and above the separate Rs 2 lakh commission he had paid to the company's partner.Even after receiving the money, the builder did not hand over the property. Instead, the man;s mother was informed that construction remained incomplete and that work had been halted because of litigation. The builder assured her that possession would be given once the work was finished.The man expected the builder to hand over the flat once the litigation was resolved. However, after waiting for another three years, he travelled to Patna in 2011 and visited the builder's office with his sister to seek an update on possession.According to the allegations, a director of the construction company refused to hand over the property and demanded an additional Rs 20 lakh before granting possession. The director also allegedly threatened them. Following this incident, the man lodged a first information report (FIR) at Kotwali Police Station.In June 2012, the man was again asked to come to Patna to take possession of the flat. But when he reached the office, the builder and the director allegedly insisted that he withdraw the criminal case and pay another Rs 20 lakh. They cited an increase in the flat's valuation as the reason for the additional demand.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleWhy did the homebuyer get relief in the consumer commission?In its written response, the builder and the construction company claimed that the dispute over the project's construction was pending before the High Court when they sent the man three registered letters asking him to clear the outstanding amount under the agreement.They alleged that he did not respond to these communications. Consequently, the builder claimed to have cancelled the allotment and terminated the agreement through a letter in 2008.After considering the submissions from both sides, the Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Patna noted that the builder had not specified when construction was completed or when the flat became ready for possession.The commission also found that the homebuyer had paid a total of Rs 15 lakh, substantially more than the agreed purchase price of Rs 10.41 lakh. Despite receiving this amount, the builder had withheld possession, citing the alleged non-payment of Rs 1,41,250.The commission held that this conduct amounted to an unfair trade practice. It also rejected the builder's claim regarding the three letters allegedly sent to the homebuyer, describing the documents relating to cancellation of the allotment and termination of the agreement as false, concocted and manufactured.The builder and the construction company had also failed to clarify what had happened to the flat or whether it had subsequently been sold to another buyer at a higher price. Commenting on their conduct, the commission observed: “The conduct of opposite parties has been unjust, unfair, dishonest, immoral, unethical and fraudulent.”Also Read | Tenant claims protection from eviction under unregistered rent agreement signed by owner's brother; Madras High Court denies saying he failed to prove tenancy and was an unlawful occupantObserving that the builder had taken undue advantage of the man’s residence outside India, the Bihar Consumer Commission directed the builder, the construction company and its director to provide the following relief:Refund Rs 15 lakh: Return the amount deposited by the homebuyer, along with 12% interest calculated from the respective date of deposit until payment. The refund was to be made within 60 days.Pay Rs 10 lakh as compensation: Compensate the man for the harassment and mental agony he endured.Pay Rs 2 lakh towards litigation costs: Reimburse the expenses incurred in pursuing the case.Bhargav KS, Managing Partner at K.S & B.K.S Law Associates, Bengaluru, told ET that the buyer's case was strengthened by the payment receipts, the agreement acknowledging receipt of Rs 9 lakh and the additional payments that the builder had not disputed.“Importantly, it did not merely treat the cancellation correspondence as unproven: it expressly held the letters fabricated, unserved and legally ineffective.” Bhargav added that the builder's failure to reveal the flat's current status, along with its deliberate absence from the proceedings after the case was remanded, further influenced the commission's assessment of its conduct.Also Read | Father got 3 bigha of land from Himachal government, but patta was never signed; why HC allowed married daughter's inheritance appeal & what role Hindu Succession Act playsYou use AI every day. articles.title: India, Canada sign fresh business deals as both sides conclude CEPA by end of 2026
articles.summary: Indian and Canada signed a series of commercial agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on Friday, as companies from both nations explore
articles.body: Indian and Canada signed a series of commercial agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on Friday, as companies from both nations explore opportunities for collaboration. The agreements were signed during the Canada-India Business Ceremony in Karnataka on Friday, attended by Canada's minister of international trade, Maninder Sidhu, who took part in the proceedings.The MoUs come as India and Canada aim to conclude negotiations for a proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of 2026. According to a presentation by the ministry of commerce and industry on Thursday, both countries have reaffirmed the deadline for completing negotiations on the proposed trade pact.The fifth round of negotiations was held in Ottawa from October 5 to October 9, with discussions covering market access for goods and services, investment parameters, rules of origin, intellectual property rights and trade remedies. The next round is scheduled to take place in New Delhi in early November.The proposed CEPA aims to lower trade barriers and improve market access for businesses in both countries. Bilateral trade between India and Canada stood at $7,956.43 million in FY26, according to government data.Official estimates suggest the agreement could increase bilateral trade by $4.4 billion to $6.5 billion. Canada is also projected to gain $3.8 billion to $5.9 billion in gross domestic product by 2035.Opportunities for Canadian businesses in IndiaSpeaking at a business reception in Bengaluru on Thursday, organised as part of the Team Canada Trade Mission to India, Sidhu highlighted the country's potential as a commercial market for Canadian companies.He pointed to artificial intelligence, quantum computing, aviation infrastructure, digital innovation, sustainability and smart mobility as areas where businesses from the two countries could work together."Canada and India are renowned for their creative flair. So what better place for all of us to gather than here in India's Innovation Hub?" Sidhu said.He also highlighted the existing presence of Canadian companies in India, including Kinaxis, OpenText, CGI, CAE, Magellan Aerospace, MDA Space and BCE Global Tech."Companies of every size are succeeding here, and it always starts with a relationship," he said.Aviation and transport were among the other areas Sidhu discussed, referring to his visit to Terminal 2 of Bengaluru airport and its planned expansion."I saw the opportunity for Canada and India to work together just a few hours ago when I toured Terminal 2 of the Bengaluru airport and heard about its plans for its expansion," he said."Canada's Fairfax Financial has already shown what it can do with its investments in the airport, and Canadian companies such as Genetec, Transoft Solutions, and RBH Access are already working hard on the ground at the airport," Sidhu added.Canada's plans to double non-US exportsSidhu also outlined Canada's ambition to double its exports to markets outside the US over the next decade, identifying India as a market Canadian companies could not afford to overlook.He said businesses were looking to bring technology, innovation and long-term partnerships to India, with potential opportunities extending across digital innovation and security, aviation infrastructure, sustainability and smart mobility, alongside artificial intelligence and quantum computing."Canadian companies like those here tonight are ready to tap into the talent to bring technology and innovation and long-term partnerships to India's dynamic market. In AI and quantum computing, in digital innovation and security, in aviation infrastructure, and in sustainability and smart mobility--and that's just the short list," he said.Sidhu cited India's economic growth, population and expected rise to become the world's third-largest economy as factors underpinning its importance to Canada's export ambitions.You use AI every day. articles.title: BMW sales in UP surge 34%, company eyes Varanasi expansion ahead of assembly polls
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Uttar Pradesh is emerging as a fast-growing luxury car market, with BMW recording 34% sales growth in the state against 10% nationally, prompting
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Uttar Pradesh is emerging as a fast-growing luxury car market, with BMW recording 34% sales growth in the state against 10% nationally, prompting the German automaker to explore expanding its dealership network to Varanasi. The company also sees potential for increased demand ahead of the upcoming UP assembly elections.In an interview with TOI, BMW Group India president and CEO Hardeep Singh Brar said rising prosperity, improved road infrastructure and growing demand among younger buyers were driving luxury car sales in UP."While our national growth is just 10%, here we are growing by almost 34%," Brar said, adding that BMW's average annual growth over the past five years exceeded 15%.BMW sold around 875 cars in UP last year and expects to cross the 1,000-unit mark for the first time in 2026, potentially reaching 1,100 units.UP currently has four BMW dealerships, located in Noida, Agra, Kanpur and Lucknow, making it the only state where the company has a presence across four cities, Brar said."We are now exploring expansion even in Varanasi," he said, clarifying that the proposal concerns a dealership, not manufacturing.Brar said BMW has been present in Lucknow since 2012 and claimed the company leads the luxury electric vehicle segment in UP.Asked whether the approaching assembly elections could boost demand, particularly among politicians who traditionally prefer large SUVs, Brar said the potential existed.He cited three factors: growing prosperity, improved highways and an expanding younger customer base."If politicians go in a BMW, they will stand out in the crowd," he remarked, suggesting that the brand could attract attention during election campaigns.Brar said around 80% of BMW customers purchase vehicles through financing rather than outright payment.However, the company has no immediate plans to establish a manufacturing facility in UP.Brar said BMW's existing Chennai facility has an annual capacity of 50,000 vehicles.For UP to attract automobile manufacturers, he emphasised developing a strong supplier ecosystem, vendor parks, logistics infrastructure and attractive tax incentives.He said improved road connectivity had already transformed cities such as Lucknow and Varanasi, strengthening their potential as luxury automobile markets.You use AI every day. articles.title: Loan seekers sharing bank data 3x more likely to get business loans: Study
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Borrowers with no credit history were more than three times as likely to get a business loan of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 25 lakh through lenders using the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Borrowers with no credit history were more than three times as likely to get a business loan of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 25 lakh through lenders using the Account Aggregator (AA) framework than through conventional channels, a study by CRIF Credit Information Services and industry alliance Sahamati showed.New-to-credit borrowers accounted for 28.5% of loans in this category disbursed by AA-enabled lenders in the 12 months ended June 2026, compared with 8.6% for other lenders. In personal loans, first-time borrowers accounted for 9% of AA-enabled originations against 3.8% through conventional channels.The report, titled “Consent to Credit: The Digital Way”, examines how consent-based financial data sharing is changing retail and MSME lending using credit bureau data.The AA framework facilitated an estimated Rs 3.82 lakh crore in loan disbursals across 3.68 crore accounts in FY26. It accounted for 8.4% of retail and MSME lending by value and 11.8% by volume, equivalent to around 1.1% of India’s GDP.As of Aug 2026, the ecosystem had 16 operational AAs, 176 financial information providers and 1,144 financial information users regulated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA. More than 566 million consents had been fulfilled, while retail users had linked over 338 million bank accounts. Banks accounted for 47.3% of AA-enabled lending by value in the second half of FY26, with NBFCs accounting for the remaining 52.7%.The framework allows lenders to access machine-readable financial data directly from banks with borrowers’ consent, replacing physical documents, PDF uploads and screen-scraping. This enables them to assess repayment capacity using actual cash flows rather than relying mainly on credit histories.AA-enabled personal loans had an average ticket size of Rs 2.7 lakh, compared with Rs 1.8 lakh through conventional channels. Average auto loan sizes were Rs 8.1 lakh against Rs 6.8 lakh, while two-wheeler loans averaged Rs 1.2 lakh against Rs 1 lakh.Lenders using AA also recorded faster portfolio growth. Over the two years ended June 2026, their housing and property loan portfolios grew at a compound annual growth rate of 32.9%, compared with 14.3% for other lenders. Active housing loan accounts increased 26.6% against 10.2%.In personal loans, AA-enabled lenders recorded portfolio growth of 30.9% annually, while active loan accounts rose 7.9%. Non-AA lenders recorded a 2% contraction in active accounts.Portfolio expansion coincided with lower or stable delinquencies. In two-wheeler loans, the share of loans overdue by more than 90 days fell to 0.5% for AA-enabled originations, compared with 5.3% for conventional loans.For business loans below Rs 10 lakh, the corresponding delinquency rates were 4.1% for AA loans and 4.4% for other loans. Personal loan delinquencies stood at 2% and 2.2%, respectively. Lenders are also using recurring consent to monitor borrower balances before EMI due dates to reduce payment failures and manage collections.The framework has expanded lending in smaller towns. Tier-3 and smaller centres accounted for 47.5% of business loan value originated through AA, compared with 32.9% through conventional channels. Their share was 40.1% in loans against property, against 25%, and 36.8% in home loans, compared with 31.5%.The report also draws on research by CAFRAL, promoted by RBI, which examined the economic effects of the nationwide AA rollout. Using satellite-recorded night-time light intensity as a proxy for economic activity, researchers found that pincodes with greater exposure to the rollout recorded a 2.11% increase in local economic activity. The impact rose to 3.03% at the district level, suggesting that easier access to credit for informal and borrowers with limited credit histories can support wider economic activity.You use AI every day. articles.title: America depends too much on China for essential minerals. We need to dig our future
articles.summary: Graphite Creek in Alaska holds the largest known U.S. graphite deposit, yet China still dominates the critical mineral supply chain America depends on.
articles.body: For decades, Americans have thought about national security primarily in terms of military strength — the aircraft we build, the ships we deploy and the men and women who defend our country. Today, national security means much more, including having access to the critical materials required to not only build our military systems, but also power our data centers, manufacture advanced technologies and support the industries that underpin the American economy. And on that front, the United States has allowed itself to become dangerously dependent on foreign nations — most notably the People’s Republic of China. CORPORATE AMERICA'S CHINA ADDICTION HAS BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT We have seen the consequences of this kind of dependence before. During the COVID-19 pandemic, disruptions in overseas supply chains left American hospitals scrambling for masks, gloves and other basic medical equipment produced in China, which controlled their distribution. It was a stark reminder that when a country outsources production of essential goods, it also outsources a measure of its security. CHINA HAS A CHOKEHOLD ON YOUR MEDICINE CABINET. IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT The COVID crisis also exposed America’s larger strategic vulnerability regarding critical minerals. Graphite is a prime example. WEST VIRGINIA UNIVERSITY RESEARCHERS TURN POLLUTED MINE WATER INTO CRITICAL RARE EARTH MINERALS Most Americans rarely think about graphite beyond being something like lead in a pencil. Yet it is an essential material in rechargeable batteries used in electric vehicles, energy storage systems and countless electronic devices. It also has applications across defense technologies, drones, advanced manufacturing and the rapidly expanding infrastructure required to support artificial intelligence and data centers. China has spent decades building dominant positions across critical mineral supply chains, from mining and processing to advanced materials manufacturing. More recently, Beijing has demonstrated that it is willing to restrict exports of strategically important materials as geopolitical and economic leverage. America should take that message seriously. RESOURCE-RICH NATION PRAISES US TIES AMID WASHINGTON-BEIJING CRITICAL MINERALS RACE No great nation should allow a strategic competitor to control the materials required to power its economy and defend itself. But despite graphite’s importance, the United States remains dependent on foreign sources, including China, for its supply. What makes this situation particularly frustrating is that America does not lack natural resources, notably in the great state of Alaska. TRUMP ANNOUNCES MASSIVE OIL, GAS AND MINERAL EXPLORATION PLANS IN GREENLAND, TOUTS NATIONAL SECURITY BENEFITS Alaska alone contains 57 of the 60 minerals identified as critical to America’s economic and national security. And on Alaska’s Seward Peninsula sits Graphite Creek, which could become the foundation of a fully integrated domestic graphite supply chain. Graphite Creek represents the kind of strategic American resource that should fundamentally change the conversation about U.S. dependence on foreign sources. The U.S. Geological Survey has recognized it as the largest known graphite deposit in the United States and among the largest in the world, making it a national security asset. But extracting the resource is only part of the solution. During the COVID-19 pandemic, disruptions in overseas supply chains left American hospitals scrambling for masks, gloves and other basic medical equipment produced in China, which controlled their distribution. America cannot simply replace foreign mines while remaining dependent on foreign processing, where, again, China dominates. A truly secure supply chain must extend from the resources in the ground through processing and into the advanced materials required by American manufacturers. The objective is straightforward: American resources, processed and manufactured in America, for American industry and national security. The challenge is not what America has beneath its feet. The challenge is our ability — and willingness — to responsibly develop it. SEN KEVIN CRAMER: CHINA BUILDS FOR WAR WHILE AMERICA WAITS ON PERMITS For decades, lengthy permitting processes, regulatory uncertainty and insufficient investment in domestic processing have made it extraordinarily difficult to bring major American mining and manufacturing projects into production. As a result, instead of producing these materials domestically under American environmental, labor and safety standards, the United States has increasingly imported them from countries where those standards may be considerably lower. That is neither sound environmental policy nor sound national security policy. America has the resources, engineering expertise, workforce and private capital necessary to dramatically reduce its dependence on foreign critical minerals. What is needed now is the resolve to do it. That means responsibly developing American resources. It means building processing and advanced materials manufacturing capacity here at home. It means creating predictable and efficient permitting processes without abandoning rigorous environmental standards. AMERICAN BUSINESSES AREN’T ALLOWED TO BUILD. IT’S TIME CONGRESS HELPED THEM Washington has increasingly recognized the importance of critical minerals, and that recognition is encouraging. But recognition must now translate into action. America cannot spend another decade studying its dependence while other countries continue strengthening their control over the world’s critical mineral supply chains. We know the vulnerability exists. We know where many of the resources are. We have the technology to develop them responsibly. No great nation should allow a strategic competitor to control the materials required to power its economy and defend itself. But despite graphite’s importance, the United States remains dependent on foreign sources, including China, for its supply. Now we need to build. The United States became the world’s leading economic and military power in large part because generations before us established the world’s greatest domestic industrial base. They understood that America’s ability to produce the materials, technologies and infrastructure it needed was inseparable from America’s strength. That principle is just as important today.
