articles.title: How much gold and silver can you keep at home without tax trouble? 500g for married women, 250g for unmarried women and 100g for men and why they are not tax-free limits
articles.summary: How much gold and silver can you legally keep at home? Is there a legal limit?
articles.body: How much gold and silver can you legally keep at home? Is there a legal limit? There is no legally prescribed upper limit on the quantity of gold or silver a person can hold at home or in a bank locker, says Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana. What matters is whether the assets were acquired lawfully and whether the owner can explain how they came into their possession.In a recent case before the ITAT Mumbai, the Income Tax Department carried out searches at a woman's residence and bank lockers, and seized diamonds, gold and silver articles, along with jewellery, which it treated as unexplained assets.The seized items included gold jewellery of 427.71 grams, 258 grams of pure gold, diamond-studded jewellery containing 161.33 grams of gold, and articles made of a silver mixture weighing 11.200 kg, according to an ET report.Also Read | Gold at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is pushing middle-class Indian buyers to silver who are getting 650 grams of silver at the same price; some betting silver at Rs 2.3 lakh per kg may hit Rs 4 lakhWhen the tax authorities questioned her about how she had acquired these assets, the woman explained that her jewellery and gold holdings had built up over several decades.She attributed it to gifts that she received at the time of marriage, streedhan, inheritance, and also customary presents from family members and purchases. She had been married for more than 35 years.To support her explanation, she also submitted details showing that the family's combined gross total income across the five assessment years under consideration was approximately Rs 4.55 crore.The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) accepted her explanation only in part. In doing so, the officer referred to CBDT Instruction No. 1916, which sets out indicative quantities of gold jewellery that may ordinarily be accepted during an income-tax search: 500 grams for a married woman, 250 grams for an unmarried woman and 100 grams for a male family member, for the purpose of seizure.The woman secured partial relief before the ITAT Mumbai, specifically on the issue concerning the jewellery and gold holdings.The tribunal observed that it was inconsistent to accept ordinary gold jewellery and diamond-studded gold jewellery as part of the family's holdings while treating pure gold as unexplained merely because it was in a different physical form.It also held that the absence of old purchase bills, by itself, was not conclusive evidence against the woman, given her explanation that the assets had accumulated through marriage gifts, inheritance and several decades of ownership.The ITAT Mumbai further clarified that CBDT Instruction No. 1916 does not establish an absolute exemption from tax or prescribe a statutory upper limit on how much jewellery a person may own.Instead, the quantities mentioned in the instruction serve as practical benchmarks to help determine whether the jewellery held by a family can reasonably be regarded as explained.At the same time, the tribunal made it clear that its finding concerning pure gold was based on the specific facts of this case. The decision should not be interpreted as establishing a general rule that all gold bullion or pure gold automatically qualifies for the treatment provided under CBDT Instruction No. 1916.Also Read | She bought gold at a discount of Rs 5,000 per 10 grams, took no receipt: How Indians are turning to under-the-counter cash deals as gold prices soar, bagging discounts of up to 6%How much gold and silver jewellery can you keep?Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET: “Any quantity may be possessed, provided its acquisition is lawful, and the person can satisfactorily explain its source.”In the case of gold jewellery, CBDT Instruction No. 1916 sets out indicative quantities that may be considered while deciding whether jewellery should be seized during an income-tax search. These are 500 grams for a married woman, 250 grams for an unmarried woman and 100 grams for a male family member.However, these quantities do not guarantee that gold within the specified limits will automatically be exempt from tax scrutiny. Surana says: “These limits should not be regarded as absolute tax-free ownership thresholds as the judicial authorities may still require explanations for their source.”The position is different for silver articles, as the instruction does not expressly specify any quantitative benchmark for them. In a case before the ITAT Mumbai, the tribunal accepted 11.2 kg of silver-mix articles after taking into account the woman's long marriage, the customary accumulation of valuables, inheritance and the family's financial position.The tribunal's decision was based on the specific circumstances of that case. It should not be interpreted as establishing a general limit on the quantity of silver that individuals can keep.For those holding substantial amounts of gold, silver or bullion, Surana advises retaining whatever documents or other reasonable evidence are available to establish how the assets were acquired. Such evidence could support a claim that the holdings came from purchases, inheritance, gifts or long-standing ownership within the family.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Katie Zacharia’s firing was foreshadowed by a chilly Fox News reception
articles.summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia’s first week was all about Katie Zacharia, when the role should have been about the president and his agenda.
articles.body: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia’s first week was all about Katie Zacharia, when the role should have been about the president and his agenda. On Friday afternoon, one week after President Donald Trump hired her, he fired her. A pair of tough Fox News interviews foreshadowed Zacharia’s change in fortune, and they were almost as awkward as her Tuesday debut in the press briefing room. Both interviews were with Fox stars who have long, friendly histories with Trump – and their questions reflected serious skepticism about Zacharia’s ability to represent the president going forward. Zacharia might have thought the Fox appearances would rehab her in the eyes of the president and the pro-Trump viewing audience. Instead, Zacharia was on the defensive, most starkly on Thursday night when Sean Hannity – a friend and informal advisor to the president – repeatedly challenged her. Hannity called Zacharia’s all-too-brief debut press briefing “widely panned.” She defended herself by admitting she had “very little prep time” since Trump offered her the job during their first in-person meeting about it. Hannity sounded like he was belatedly vetting Zacharia for the job — unintentionally highlighting Trump’s lack of vetting. The president’s Truth Social post appointing Zacharia called her “an attorney,” but she failed the bar exam, a fact she acknowledged to Hannity on Thursday night. CNN’s Andrew Kaczynski has shown how Zacharia repeatedly amplified stories and posts identifying her as an attorney in recent years. The issue ultimately comes down to credibility, an essential attribute for any press secretary. “Between her lying about being an attorney and that humiliating debut, I have to imagine her West Wing colleagues are absolutely livid,” Sarah Matthews told CNN Thursday night. Matthews served as deputy press secretary in the Trump White House until resigning the night of the January 6, 2021 attack. “Karoline Leavitt was doing that job while pregnant and was ruthlessly efficient at it,” Matthews said. “Now, much of that involved lying and gaslighting the American public, but she knew how to command a briefing room. And if Zacharia can’t even handle a Hannity interview? She is in for a rough ride.” White House communications director Steven Cheung publicly defended Zacharia as “uniquely qualified and whip smart.” On Wednesday, he wrote, “At the end of this second term, she’ll be remembered as one of the all-time greats.” As White House officials anonymously questioned how long Zacharia will remain in the role, Trump detractors drew parallels to Anthony Scaramucci’s infamous 11-day stint as White House communications director in 2017. “Records are made to be broken,” Scaramucci quipped Friday afternoon on X. “But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.” Conservative commentators did not hold back their criticism either. Podcaster Meghan McCain said Friday morning that Zacharia shouldn’t be anywhere near a briefing room. “One of the biggest problems with the administration right now is every issue facing Americans is serious and all they do is keep hiring deeply unserious people to represent them,” McCain wrote on X. “It gives the impression the administration just simply doesn’t care what Americans think and that their problems aren’t worth hiring capable people with real experience.” Zacharia’s predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, held one press briefing a week on average. Leavitt stepped down in August, shortly after returning from maternity leave. Fox News recently hired her as an on-air contributor. Zacharia was announced as Leavitt’s successor last Friday, hours after she flew to Washington to meet with Trump about the position. The president cited her “unblemished record of support” for his presidency and her regular TV appearances. Zacharia’s cable news credentials are well-established. She was a popular MAGA defender on cable, including on CNN, while living in California with her family. However, representing the US from the White House podium requires a different skill set. In Thursday interviews, Zacharia rather candidly said she might not have been ready for her briefing room debut. Talking with Jack Posobiec, the “Pizzagate” conspiracy theorist who now hosts on the pro-Trump streaming channel Real America’s Voice, Zacharia said she “never had a full briefing beforehand.” It was a whirlwind hiring process, Zacharia said, starting with an unexpected call from the president on Wednesday, October 7: “Wednesday phone call; Thursday flight; Friday meeting; Saturday flight; Sunday flight; Monday, Columbus Day, federal holiday. Start work, wants a brief Tuesday morning.” While Zacharia didn’t say so, the implication was that Trump wanted her out there and on camera as soon as possible. Zacharia read pro-Trump talking points, then called on three reporters — one asked about Kimberly Guilfoyle, then the embattled US ambassador to Greece, which led Zacharia to announce that the president had asked Guilfoyle to resign. Speaking with Hannity, Zacharia touted that moment: “I delivered some breaking news. I think I’m one of the first press secretaries to deliver staff changes for the administration, and I was honored that President Trump trusted me delivering that information.” Hannity, a close confidant of the president, sounded unimpressed with her press briefing performance and her answers on Thursday night. As the TV segment’s outro music began to play, indicating Zacharia was out of time, she tried to reassure Hannity: “I will be very prepared, Sean, and I will step up to the duty President Trump has asked me to as press secretary.” Later in the evening, Trump indicated he had watched the broadcast because he posted on Truth Social praising one of Hannity’s other guests. On Friday morning, “Fox & Friends” co-host (and Hannity’s fiancée) Ainsley Earhardt referenced the previous interview and expressed sympathy for Zacharia. “You were just thrown into this role,” she remarked. “Fox & Friends” interviews with Trump administration officials are often genial, but Earhardt’s fellow co-hosts appeared skeptical. “It’s been a tough week for you,” Lawrence Jones said to her. Jones asked whether she wished she had told the president she never passed the bar exam — a fact that emerged amid days of press scrutiny of her background. “Those questions weren’t asked,” she said. “I’m being hired as White House press secretary, not White House counsel.” Even as the Fox hosts — known for their Trump boosterism — scrutinized her credentials and credibility, Zacharia pivoted to blaming the “legacy media,” arguing that unnamed other outlets want to “put the focus and attention on me” because they “want to be distracted from the major wins that President Trump is making for America.” When Earhardt asked when the next press briefing would be, Zacharia didn’t say. Then Jones asked: “Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?” “I’m standing here,” Zacharia responded, referring to the fact that she was live from the White House North Lawn. When the interview ended, Zacharia said hello to a crowd of reporters gathered outside, but declined to answer any questions. “I’m not taking any questions, but I wanted to let you know I’m looking forward to working with all of you so much,” she said. “Please get my number, reach out to me, call me, text me, email me.” Matthews told CNN that Zacharia should have waited to hold her first briefing “until she felt adequately prepared.” “Karoline Leavitt was doing that job while pregnant and was ruthlessly efficient at it,” Matthews said. “Now, much of that involved lying and gaslighting the American public, but she knew how to command a briefing room. And if Zacharia can’t even handle a Hannity interview? She is in for a rough ride.”

articles.title: Aldi planned 180 new stores for 2026. The newest are about to open
articles.summary: More than 180 new Aldi stores were expected to open this year, and several of those are gearing up to welcome shoppers just in time for the holidays.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – More than 180 new Aldi stores were expected to open this year, and several of those are gearing up to welcome shoppers just in time for the holidays .

The international discount supermarket chain revealed in January that it planned to open dozens of new locations throughout the U.S. with the goal of “making it even easier for customers to shop our aisles first,” CEO Atty McGrath said in a press release.

It wasn’t clear at the time, however, where exactly Aldi would expand to. The grocer did share that the supermarkets would open in 31 states, with 80 alone planned for the Southeast.

Among the locations that opened this year was Maine’s first-ever Aldi, located in Portland.

Multiple stores, listed below, celebrated grand openings this week, according to Aldi’s website.

Prescott Valley , Arizona – 3330 North Glassford Hill Road

Metairie , Louisiana – 215 Veterans Memorial Boulevard

Lansing , Michigan – 2110 Lake Lansing Road

Glen Allen , Virginia – 10310 Washington Highway

Even more are on track to open this month. Customers can get a sneak peek of new stores in Mesa , Arizona (6853 East Elliot Road), and Poughkeepsie , New York (3456 North Road), on Oct. 21, with grand opening events set for Oct. 22.

Later this month, Aldi will open new stores in North Little Rock , Arkansas (11201 Maumelle Boulevard), and Bristol , Connecticut (1235 Farmington Avenue). Sneak peeks are set for Oct. 28, with grand opening events the following day, according to Aldi. The new stores coming to Madison (729 West Base Street) and Zephyrhills (38901 County Road 54), Florida, do not have sneak peek events scheduled, webpages show.

As of October 2026, Aldi has more than 2,700 stores across the U.S. Florida has the most of any state at 346, followed by Illinois at 217 and Pennsylvania at 174.

Ten states do not have an Aldi store: Alaska, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming.

For Colorado, however, the lack of Aldi locations is expected to end soon. Nexstar’s KDVR reported in January that Aldi had plans to bring 50 stores to Colorado over the next few years. In July, Aldi submitted concept plans for two locations near Denver , according to KDVR.

By the end of 2028, Aldi hopes to have a footprint of 3,200 stores.

Nexstar’s Michael Bartiromo contributed to this report.

articles.title: Warsh offers no fresh signals on interest rates
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined Friday to predict central bank officials’ future course on interest rates, less than two weeks before they meet to discuss monetary policy. “I don’t prejudge meetings. I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year,” Warsh…
articles.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined Friday to predict central bank officials’ future course on interest rates, less than two weeks before they meet to discuss monetary policy.

“I don’t prejudge meetings. I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year,” Warsh told Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), in Bangkok, Thailand.

Officials on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), including Warsh, voted unanimously last month to raise interest rates by a quarter point to a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent.

After that vote, Warsh said the hike was an attempt to tame inflation , which has exceeded the Fed’s 2 percent target for more than five years.

Yet Warsh has taken a cautious approach toward issuing forward guidance during his five months leading the central bank, a stance he argues will allow markets to operate according to indicators from the economy, not the Fed.

“It’s a new chapter at the Fed and … we’re not in that business anymore,” Warsh told Georgieva, referring to forecasting future decisions.

Georgieva then quipped that the Fed chair “just disappointed half of the audience, or more,” to laughs from the crowd at the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank Group.

Multiple FOMC officials have recently indicated that additional rate hikes are on the way, while acknowledging they must evaluate incoming economic data. The panel will meet Oct. 27-28 and release its rates decision on the latter day.

Fed board member Christopher Waller said last week he anticipates future rate hikes “if the economic data continue to come in” as he expects.

“But there is some flexibility about when those hikes will occur,” he said at the Istanbul Economic Forum in Turkey.

Waller made those comments before the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that annual inflation was 3.7 percent in September , 0.3 percentage points higher than it was in August .

Energy price pressures due to the Iran war and Russia-Ukraine conflict remain. A gallon of regular gas in the U.S. costs roughly $4.33 on average as of Friday, according to AAA .

Rising demand for artificial intelligence models and data centers is also pushing up inflation, as Warsh acknowledged in Thailand . The Fed chair said the advent of AI is “probably the most consequential change” to the U.S. and global economies of his lifetime.

In the medium term, Warsh predicted AI would spur a “positive supply shock,” increasing productivity and wealth for countries that “put it to good use.”

The Fed chair added, “The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one. Bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don’t know what the market structure’s going to be of these new technologies.”

articles.title: Main Trump legal fund $1.9M in debt
articles.summary: President Trump’s primary legal fund is more than $1.9 million in debt, according to its latest filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Save America PAC, which Trump formed after he lost the 2020 presidential election, spent more than $5.4 million in the third quarter and had spent more than $14 million from the start…
articles.body:
President Trump’s primary legal fund is more than $1.9 million in debt, according to its latest filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC).

Save America PAC, which Trump formed after he lost the 2020 presidential election, spent more than $5.4 million in the third quarter and had spent more than $14 million from the start of the year through September, per its quarterly filing to the FEC .

At the start of the year, the president had nearly $1.2 million on hand. The fund had roughly $673,000 as of the end of June . But as of the end of the third quarter, it had less than $33,000.

The PAC also owes more than $1.9 million to legal firms and received roughly $4.7 million in transfers from Never Surrender PAC, another Trump-affiliated group, from July through September.

The Hill has reached out to a spokesperson for MAGA Inc., another super PAC that supports the president.

Save America lists all the debts it holds as legal consulting or legal fees and expenses. They range from about $239,000 owed to Brito PLLC — whose founder, Alejandro Brito, represented the president in multiple lawsuits he filed against ABC News , BBC and other media outlets.

In the defamation suit against ABC, the company agreed to settle by providing $15 million for Trump’s future presidential library.

Save America also owes about $760,000 to Sullivan & Cromwell LLP, which is representing Trump in his appeal of a New York jury’s 2024 ruling convicting him on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records .

Dhillon Law Group, which Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon founded in 2006, is owed $34,000. Dhillon, who runs the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Civil Rights Division, departed the firm when she officially joined the administration last year.

The fund’s debts decreased in the third quarter, as the PAC reported owing more than $3.7 million at the end of the second quarter. The amount the organization owes to Brito’s firm and Sullivan & Cromwell rose from nearly $169,000 and roughly $335,600 as of the end of the second quarter, respectively, according to the FEC .

Its obligations to Dhillon Law Group, meanwhile, decreased from roughly $96,500 as of the end of the second quarter.

articles.title: Oil prices jump sharply, to nearly $110 per barrel
articles.summary: Oil prices jumped sharply Friday to their highest levels in weeks, as investors assessed the impact of both the Iran and Ukraine-Russia wars on global energy.
articles.body: Oil prices jumped sharply Friday to their highest levels in weeks, as investors assessed the impact of both the Iran and Ukraine-Russia wars on global energy supplies. Brent crude oil spiked above $109 per barrel, its highest level since mid-September. The oil price benchmark — widely considered to be among the most important figures in global energy — was just a few cents away from its highest level in five months. U.S. crude oil, which also steers gas prices, rose to $100 per barrel. It was the first time West Texas Intermediate crude had crossed that threshold, closely watched by both traders and the public, since September. Friday’s price jumps will likely add to already elevated gasoline prices for U.S. consumers in coming days. As of Friday morning, regular gasoline averaged $4.32 per gallon nationwide. At midafternoon trading levels, oil prices were poised to gain about 5% over the course of the week. Diesel futures also jumped by more than 1% Friday. The cost of this commercial fuel critical for farming and other industrial sectors has risen even faster than regular gasoline in recent months. Stocks fell Friday, partly in response to the jump in energy prices. The S&P 500 fell more than 1% while the Nasdaq Composite sharply dropped 2% by midafternoon. The price of fuel around the world began its steady rise this spring, when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February, prompting the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. But an escalation in the Russia-Ukraine war in recent months has caused an even more dramatic price spike for diesel. Russia has traditionally been one of the world’s largest diesel exporters. But attack by Ukrainian forces on its energy infrastructure has taken much of its refining capacity offline. Likewise, energy assets in Ukraine have been targeted by Russian strikes. As a result of the strikes, buyers of Russian diesel have been forced to look elsewhere for their fuel supplies. But there aren’t any clear opportunities to easily expand diesel production. Refineries in the U.S. and Europe are already running at nearly maximum capacity to churn out as much diesel fuel as possible. President Donald Trump is intensely focused on the high cost of diesel fuel because of its key role in driving up inflation -- a top issue for American voters in the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Trump has pressured U.S. allies to release some of their diesel and crude oil reserves, and he recently signed an order to ease regulations on the use of off-road “red dye” diesel. When neither of these actions resulted in a significant step down for diesel prices, Trump made the decision this month to ease U.S. sanctions on Russia. The goal was to allow Russian President Vladimir Putin to release some of Russia’s supplies to the global market. But the sanctions relief stunned world leaders and drew quick condemnation from U.S. lawmakers in both parties. While Trump has touted the deal with Putin as a way to lower prices, as of Friday, no actual Russian diesel had been identified as having reached the global market. Russia’s refining infrastructure has been badly damaged by Ukrainian strikes. On Friday, another Russian refiner suspended some crude oil operations. The Russian Defense Ministry said Ukraine had “attempted a massive attack on the Ryazan oil refinery.” Additionally, a group of American lawmakers introduced a bill that would block Trump’s deal for Russian diesel. It has little chance of passing the Republican-controlled House. But polling indicates that Republicans are unlikely to maintain a majority in the House after November’s elections. The Russian diesel blocking bill offers a preview of the kind of legislation that could advance under Democratic control. Yet even now, the legislation adds to “growing doubts that a U.S. — Russia diesel deal will come to fruition,” said Mason Mendez, global real assets analyst at Wells Fargo. “Investors also remain concerned about further military escalation in the Middle East, as attacks on commercial shipping and regional infrastructure have increased in recent weeks,” he said. “Looking into 2027, the need to rebuild depleted global inventories could create an addition source of demand and keep energy prices elevated for longer.”

articles.title: Fairfax-IDBI deal signals stronger Canada-India ties: Sidhu
articles.summary: Fairfax’s $5.5B IDBI Bank stake buy signals stronger Canada-India ties, boosts investor confidence and momentum for CEPA trade deal by year-end.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings’ nearly $5.5 billion investment in IDBI Bank signals improving economic ties between Canada and India and could encourage further investments, Canada’s trade minister Maninder Sidhu said in Bengaluru on Friday, as the two countries work towards concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of the year.The transaction, involving the acquisition of a majority stake in IDBI Bank, will be the largest foreign investment in India’s financial sector, Sidhu said. “It’s the largest deal between our two countries in the financial sector, and that sends a clear signal to supply chains that Canada is ready to do more,” he said.Canadian pension funds and large institutions have collectively invested close to C$107 billion in India across roads, highways, healthcare, technology, clean technology and energy. Sidhu said investors were looking to expand their presence as India builds infrastructure, including highways and airports.The minister was speaking at the conclusion of a Canadian trade mission that brought around 300 business delegates representing 150 organisations to India, the largest such mission in 30 years. More than 30 deals between Canadian delegates and Indian partners, worth close to C$300 million, were concluded during the visit, he said.“When you sign a free trade agreement, the business community picks up the cues. The warming of relations between the two countries is very important,” he said.The immediate priority is CEPA, negotiations for which were relaunched in Nov last year. Five rounds have been completed, with another scheduled for the week of Nov 9 in Delhi. The agreement is expected to help more than double bilateral trade to $70 billion by 2030.Sidhu said he and commerce minister Piyush Goyal had met close to 10 times to advance negotiations. “Our goal is to conclude the agreement by the end of this year,” he said.CEPA could open up opportunities in energy, critical minerals, fertilisers, aerospace and advanced manufacturing by reducing tariffs and improving market access, Sidhu said.Citing India’s import duties of around 7-8% on potash, he said lower tariffs could make fertilisers more affordable for Indian farmers. Reduced duties on aerospace products could also bring down costs. Canada, meanwhile, has high tariffs on apparel, footwear and furniture, potentially creating opportunities for Indian exporters.“The two economies are complementary,” Sidhu said, adding that tariff lines offered clues to the sectors likely to gain most from the agreement.CEPA could also create further opportunities for Indian IT services companies in Canada, while Canadian engineering firms could contribute to India’s infrastructure development, he said.On immigration, Sidhu said Canada remained open to international students and skilled workers but wanted a more sustainable system that accounted for pressures on housing, healthcare and infrastructure.“We’re really focused on economic immigration as a government,” he said, pointing to demand for physicians and nurses in Canada’s healthcare sector.
